chapter_title: Concerning the Five Storehouses that have poured f

spiritual_reading.full_translation:
From the first rising of a state of denial, a sufficient set of interior reservoirs was opened within that domain, and from those interiors a sufficient series of fundamental perversions flowed forth. From that series, fixed systems of distorted perception were organized; and from those systems there were brought forth complete kinds of disordered affections and thoughts in every degree of life, each joined in a counterfeit union of love and understanding. In each such degree there reign a sufficient set of dominant loves, together with their persuasive spirits, their embodied habits and compulsions, and their delights of appropriation; and in each degree these differ, because each degree bears its own specific quality of evil and falsity.

The ruling love that presides over the obscuring persuasion rising from the lowest denial came up from what is most remote from heaven, and it became the head of the whole complex of malice. Through it the first spreading of spiritual conflict broke forth: contentions against truth, assaults upon good, mutual hatred, peril to what can live, and the destruction of what might be restored. It first stirred the lust of domination and opposition, together with its organized degrees and operative forces; and afterward it set itself against the influx of wisdom and rose into direct opposition to the higher government of good and truth.

In that chief ruling evil there is a full set of outward aspects that display the quality of the whole. In its highest it is a proud and cruel confidence as chief among ravenous affections; in its deeds it is the delight of doing harm and of subjugating; in what supports and carries its rule it is a lofty, far-seeing craft; in its inmost craving it is a devouring appetite to possess and consume what is another’s; and in its ultimate extension it is a cold, sensuous persuasion that drags everything down into mere outward knowing. These are the complete impressions by which that kingdom is recognized.

There is also in it a sufficient set of ruling qualities: first, the absence of wisdom that it takes for its own light; second, the corruption of every affection for good; third, the deforming of all truth into what serves self; fourth, the interior sting and bitterness that it experiences as its life; fifth, the burning zeal of self-love that inflames as if it were strength and presses forward with harsh fervor.

Further, there is in it a formed character that resists amendment: it is stiff and unyielding because it is shaped from the intention of spiritual death, from a will set against heaven. That intention makes its confirmed state hard to break by any ordinary correction, for it has been made firm by repeated acts and therefore does not easily submit.

Also, that chief ruling evil has a shrewd perception of the utterances and reasonings that arise within its subordinate degrees. It catches the sound and manner of their persuasions, understands what is exchanged among them in their various modes of falsity, and perceives the schemes and devices by which they would protect themselves or evade restraint; it even notices the silent agreements by which they consent together. Yet the subordinate forces do not likewise grasp the deeper purposes of that ruling evil, and although much is laid open to it, it does not penetrate the inner ends of others as they are in themselves; it does not know their ruling mind, nor can it comprehend the whole course of their designs from first to last. It apprehends only what is present and immediate, what lies within its current awareness.

Moreover, it can alternately expand itself into active power and contract itself into a compact, oppressive presence. When it is stirred, it sends its influences outward into many operations; when it turns back into itself, it draws its operations inward and becomes a concentrated weight among its allies, pressing downward into the lowest loves. It terrifies by the violence of its persuasive outcry and shakes its subordinate forces by asserted certainty that drowns discernment; and when it summons its own, weaker impulses and subordinate falsities fall into tremor and collapse, as thoughts without support fail under a stronger persuasion. Yet it has no true foresight: it does not perceive what is remote in consequence, nor what lies outside its immediate sphere, but attends only to what is directly before it.

These are the evil impressions found in the chief love of infernal persuasion, brought forth by a domain of denial and nourished by cruelty, wickedness, and wrath, surpassing the other ruling evils that preside in its several degrees.

In the degree where falsity is most glittering and most convincing in externals, the embodied form of that ruling evil is a show of preciousness without genuine worth, and the whole company of its subordinate forces appears in the same kind of splendor; and the delight by which it appropriates is a harsh, biting relish, because it delights in desolating and in making what is living barren.

In contrast, in the degree where self-love burns openly as dominant zeal, the ruling evil is marked by proud confidence as chief among brutish affections. Its embodied form is the hardness of outward good turned to selfish use, and the forms of its subordinate rulers are similar; and the delight by which it appropriates is a pervasive sourness, because even what seems lively in it is inwardly hostile to innocence.

Again, in the degree where persuasion is volatile and domineering in thought, the ruling evil is marked by lofty craft in reasoning. Its embodied form is rigid severity in truthless confidence, and the forms of all who belong to that persuasion are of the same kind; and the delight by which it appropriates is a sharpness that cuts, because it delights in disputation and in wounding truth.

In the degree where truth is falsified and made to serve sensuous pleasure, the ruling evil is marked by a cold, outward intelligence. Its embodied form is a pale appearance of truth without life, and the forms of its subordinate rulers are similar; and the delight by which it appropriates is a sweetness that seems gentle, because falsity mimics truth and insinuates itself pleasantly into the natural mind.

Finally, in the degree of active denial itself, the ruling evil is the devouring craving that destroys spiritual life. Its embodied form is the heaviness and baseness of what is merely ultimate, compounded of gross falsity with its dull confirmations, and the forms of all who belong to that denial are of the same kind; and the delight by which it appropriates is bitterness, because it hates good and therefore feels good as torment.

And the persuasive spirit that reigns in these states continues wherever falsity claims revelation apart from heaven: in self-derived predictions, in every kind of deceptive sign-making, in states where another’s falsity takes possession of the mind, and in all varieties of pretended inspiration that draw their voice not from the Divine but from lower loves.

spiritual_reading.overall_coherence: The chapter holds together strongly as a single fivefold anatomy of infernal degrees: interiors → fundamental perversions → organized perceptions → genera of disordered life, then the chief ruling love’s qualities, powers, limits, and finally five differentiated embodiments with their characteristic delights. Minor stumbling points are the fragmentary ¶11 and the highly physical motion imagery in ¶9, which requires smoothing into alternating modes of influence; otherwise the voice and progression are consistent.

findings.diagnosis: Clean programmatic fivefold generative schema. No narrative break: it establishes a causal chain (storehouses→elements→trees→genera→worlds/kings/spirits/bodies/tastes) that the rest of the chapter concretizes.
findings.evidence: Text teaches by what things produce: “Five storehouses… The five elements poured out of them… fashioned the five trees… fashioned the five genera… five kings… five spirits, five bodies, five tastes.” The spiritual reading notes it “OPENS — … generative structure of evil by degrees” and does not report a mismatch; later paragraphs (¶12–16) supply the promised “bodies/tastes,” confirming coherence rather than later editorial patching.

findings.diagnosis: Clean continuation: introduces the chief exemplar (King of Smoke) as causal source of war; this is narrative development, not an administrative inventory.
findings.evidence: The king is active, not merely listed: “The beginning of the spread of the war occured through him… Afterwards… he waged war with the light.” The spiritual reading tracks this as “DEVELOPS — … chief ruling evil and its first acts,” with no stumble or forced harmonization.

findings.diagnosis: Clean fivefold correspondences (shapes; properties). The five faces/properties function as diagnostic manifestations of one principle, matching the chapter’s internal fivefold pedagogy; no sign of a foreign administrative layer.
findings.evidence: Shapes are explicitly didactic: “These five shapes, the marks of his five worlds, exist on the King…” and then a second fivefold: “five other properties… darkness… putridity… ugliness… bitterness… burning.” The reading’s note that animal-to-aspect assignment is “interpretive but consistent with function” indicates the text invites correspondential mapping rather than jurisdictional ranking.

findings.diagnosis: Genuine difficulty from damage/ellipsis and a local voice wobble due to broken syntax (“even as she has formed him… namely Matter…”). The narrative does not improve by removal; it is a corrupted transmission seam, not an insertion of a different teaching mode.
findings.evidence: The paragraph’s grammar is fractured and has unclear referents: “even as she has formed him… namely Matter… [o]ne who sculpted him…”. The spiritual reading explicitly flags a structural issue: “omitted ¶7… creates a structural gap,” and smooths hardness imagery into ‘resistance to reformation’—a typical response to textual roughness rather than to alien content.

findings.diagnosis: Clean (though highly imagistic) functional description of perceptual limits and kinetic capacities of the ruler. The reader’s ‘smoothing’ reflects dense metaphor, not administrative overlay.
findings.evidence: Both paragraphs teach by capability/limitation (what he can and cannot do): “knows the converse and language… understands… knows… Yet… heart is not manifested… only knows… what is before his eyes” and “spreads all his limbs… withdraws… rolled… terrifies… Still… knows not what is far.” The spiritual reading notes only that some images “resist precise spiritual differentiation” (¶9), not that the content changes teaching mode or introduces non-participating names.

findings.diagnosis: Genuine difficulty: ¶11 is fragmentary and functions as a damaged bridge into the next section. Not an insertion; it’s a broken continuation of the supremacy motif.
findings.evidence: ¶10 offers a summary closure (“These signs… are found…”), while ¶11 is an orphaned comparative (“… more than all his fellow rulers…”). The reader calls ¶11 “fragmentary… necessarily minimal.” This is classic physical loss at a transition, not a change into governance/jurisdiction language.

findings.diagnosis: Clean five-world exemplification in correspondential mode using ‘body (metal)’ and ‘taste (fruit)’ as functional manifestations. The kings are not arranged as an administrative roster; each world is characterized by sensory/embodied qualities that the opening schema promised.
findings.evidence: Each unit follows the same functional template: king’s face → body metal → bodies of powers/rulers → taste (“Gold… salty”; “Copper… sour”; “iron… sharp”; “silver… sweetness”). The spiritual reading tracks this as a “fivefold survey… embodiment and delight,” which is precisely the functional/correspondential method, not a jurisdictional assignment of officers.

findings.diagnosis: Mixed ending: primarily correspondential (metal/taste), but it adds an application gloss identifying the reigning spirit with contemporary oracle/possession practices. This is not ‘administrative’ (no ranks/territories), but it is a recognizable didactic expansion from cosmological description to present-day polemic, likely appended as an explanatory addendum.
findings.evidence: After the established template (“body is lead and tin… taste… bitterness”), the paragraph pivots with “Again, the spirit who reigns in them is the spirit who speaks till today in the soothsayers…” This is a seam-marker (“till today”) and a shift from world-description to contemporary religious critique (soothsayers, portents, possessed). The spiritual reading treats it as “straightforward… ongoing spiritual phenomena,” which indicates it does not break the story, but it does change the discourse level (cosmic anatomy → present identification).
findings.scope: Annotate the concluding ‘till today’ application gloss in ¶16 beginning with: “Again, the spirit who reigns in them is the spirit who speaks till today in the soothsayers…” through the end of the paragraph, as a likely secondary explanatory addendum rather than the core fivefold anatomy.

textual_criticism.summary: 8 findings: 5 clean correspondential sections (¶2–5, ¶8–9, ¶12–15), 2 genuine-damage difficulties at transition points (¶6; ¶10–11), and 1 mixed-voice addendum at the end (¶16 second half) recommended for annotation (not excision). No clear administrative-inventory insertion that would make the narrative flow better if removed.

harmonized_paragraphs.text: Five storehouses have arisen since the beginning in the land of darkness! The five elements poured out of them. Also, from the five elements were fashioned the five trees! Again, from the five trees were fashioned the five genera of creatures in each world, male and female. And the five worlds themselves have five kings therein, and five spirits, five bodies, five tastes; in each world, they not resembling one another!

The King of the world of Smoke [is the ruler] who came up from the depth of darkness; this is he who is the head of all wickedness, and all malignity. The beginning of the spread of the war occured through him; all the battles, fights, quarrelling, dangers, destructions, fights, wrestling-contests! That is the one who first made arise danger and war, with his worlds and his powers. Afterwards, also, he waged war with the light. He pitched a battle with the exalted kingdom.

⟨p.31⟩
Now, regarding the King of Darkness, there are five shapes on him! His head is lion-faced; his hands and feet are demon- and devil-faced; his shoulders are eagle-faced; while his belly is dragon-faced; his tail is fish-faced. These five shapes, the marks of his five worlds, exist on the King of the realms of Darkness!

Now, there are five other properties in him. The first is his darkness. The second is his putridity. The third is his ugliness. The fourth is his bitterness, his own soul. The fifth is his burning, which burns like an iron () as if poured out from fire.

[There are] also three others in him! The first, that his body is hard and very tough, even as she has formed him [in evil and] cruel-hearted; namely Matter, who is the thought of death, [o]ne who sculpted him from the nature of the land of darkness. This is the manner of the body of the ruler of Smoke. He is harder than every iron, copper and steel and lead; as there is no cleaver at all, nor any iron implement, can [break] him and cut him. For Matter, his fashioner, has formed him [exceedingly] strong and hard.

⟨p.32⟩
The third, that the King of the realms of Darkness knows the converse and language of his five worlds. He understands every thing he hears from their mouths, as they address one another; each one of them in his language. [Every] design they will consider against him, every snare they debate with one another to bring upon him, he knows them! He can also understand the gesturing they signal between one another. Yet, his powers and his rulers, who are subject to him, can not understand his wordy converse. While all these things are unveiled to him; still, their heart is not manifested to him. He knows not their mind nor their thought; he can not ponder their beginning and their end. Rather, he only knows and apprehends what is before his eyes.

Also, another different thing is found in the King of the realms of Darkness! For when it pleases him to move, he spreads all his limbs out and walks. When it comes to mind, he with[d]raws his limbs and takes them in, and is rolled (?) to his companions; and he falls to the ground like a grape and a great iron ball! He terrifies by his cry, he is frightful. He frightens his powers with his sound; because when he speaks, being like thunder in the clouds, he resembles the [crash] of the rocks [when they are split] When he cries out and [roars] and calls [aloud] over his powers, they shall tremble and to[tter a]nd fall under foot; even as some birds would be [driven by] the bird [hawk] and they fall down to the earth. Still, this thing only: he knows not what is far from him, he sees not who is at a distance, nor does he hear him. Rather, whoever is before his face he sees, hearing him and knowing him.

These signs and these evil marks are found in the chief of the demons and fiends, the King of all the mountains of Darkness [who is the foremost of them,] to [whom] the land of darkness has given birth, begotten in its cruelty, in its wickedness and its wrath [and reared in its poison.]

⟨p.33⟩
... more than all his fellow rulers, who are in all his worlds.
Gold is the body of the King of the realms of Darkness. The body of all the powers who belong to the world of Smoke is gold. And also, the taste of its fruits is salty.

In contrast, the King of the worlds of Fire is lion-faced, the foremost of all the beasts. Copper is his body. Again, the body of all the rulers who belong to Fire is copper. Their taste is the sour taste that is in every form.
Again, the King of the worlds of Wind is eagle-face. His body is iron. Also, the body of all they who belong to the Wind is iron. Their taste is the sharp taste that is in every form.

For his part, the King of the world of Water is fish-face. His body is silver. All the other rulers who belong to Water, silver is their body. Also, the taste of their fruit is the sweetness of water, the sweet taste that is in every (form).

Again, [the Kin]g of the world of Darkness is a dragon. His [body is lead] and tin. All the other rulers [who belong to the world of] Darkness, their body is lead and tin. And also, the taste of their fruits is bitterness. Again, the spirit who reigns in them is the spirit who speaks till today in the soothsayers, giving oracles; in the givers of portents, every type; in they who are possessed; and the other spirits that give oracles, every type.

changes_summary: No changes made. The only non-core material identified by the critic is the concluding ‘till today’ application gloss in ¶16 (Finding 8), but the recommendation there is annotate (not excise), so the text remains unchanged. All other findings recommend none.
